feedback.problem:
The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is given by

$$
v=⟨-12\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,8\sqrt{t}⟩,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the particle when $t=4\,\text{s}.$ Round your final answer to one decimal place.
feedback.worked_solution:
Newton’s second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-12\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8\sqrt{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{12}{t},\,\frac{4}{\sqrt{t}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the resultant force $F$ at time $t$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =2\cdot ⟨-\frac{12}{t},\,\frac{4}{\sqrt{t}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{24}{t},\,\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=4\,\text{s},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(4) & =⟨-\frac{24}{4},\,\frac{8}{\sqrt{4}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of $F(4)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}|F(4)| & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & ≈7.2\,\text{N}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
